drivingQuestion: Does Hillel's ordinance show that, in general, giving against the recipient's will is or is not a valid giving?
outcomeNote: In both versions Rav Pappa's objection to Rava's inference is left unanswered.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רָבָא: מִתַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הַלֵּל — ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״, וּנְתָנָהּ לוֹ מִדַּעְתּוֹ — מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת, בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ — אֵינָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת.
segments.en: «GEMARA» «Rava says:» It may be inferred «from the ordinance of Hillel» in the mishna that if one says to his wife: «This is your bill of divorce on the condition that you will give me two hundred dinars, and she gave» the money to «him with his consent,» then she is «divorced.» But if she gave it to him «against his will, she is not divorced.»

segments.he: מִדְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְהִלֵּל לְתַקּוֹנֵי נְתִינָה בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ הָוְיָא נְתִינָה, הָא בְּעָלְמָא נְתִינָה בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ לָא הָוְיָא נְתִינָה.
segments.en: The Gemara elaborates: «From» the fact «that» it «was necessary for Hillel to institute» that «giving against the will» of the receiver «is» considered «giving,» in the case of houses of walled cities, one may infer «that in general, giving against the will» of the recipient «is not» considered «giving.»

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: וְדִילְמָא כִּי אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ לְהִלֵּל לְתַקּוֹנֵי שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, אֲבָל בְּפָנָיו — בֵּין מִדַּעְתּוֹ בֵּין בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ הָוְיָא מַתָּנָה!
segments.en: «Rav Pappa objects to this, and some say» that it was «Rav Ashi» who objected: «But perhaps when it was necessary for Hillel to institute» this ordinance, it was specifically for a case «where» the seller gives the money «not in» the «presence» of the buyer; «but» if he repays the buyer «in his presence,» then «whether» the buyer was repaid «with his consent or whether» it was «against his will, it is» considered a valid act of «giving.»

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: מִתַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הִלֵּל — הֲרֵי זֶה ״גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״, וּנְתָנָהּ לוֹ, בֵּין מִדַּעְתּוֹ בֵּין בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ — הָוְיָא נְתִינָה. וְכִי אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְהִלֵּל לְתַקּוֹנֵי — שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, אֲבָל בְּפָנָיו — בֵּין מִדַּעְתּוֹ בֵּין בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ הָוְיָא נְתִינָה.
segments.en: «There are» those «who say» an opposite version of this discussion, i.e., that «Rava says:» One may infer «from the ordinance of Hillel» that if one says to his wife: «This is your bill of divorce on the condition that you will give me two hundred dinars, and she gave» it «to him, whether» it was «with his consent or whether» it was «against his will, it is» a valid act of «giving. And» this is because «when it was necessary for Hillel to institute» this ordinance, it was specifically for a case «where» the seller gives the money «not in» the «presence» of the buyer. «But» if the seller repays him «in his presence, whether» the buyer was repaid «with his consent or whether» it was «against his will, it is» considered a valid act of «giving.»

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: וְדִילְמָא בֵּין בְּפָנָיו בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, מִדַּעְתּוֹ — אִין, בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ — לָא, וְהִלֵּל מַאי דְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ תַּקֵּין!
segments.en: «Rav Pappa objects to this, and some say» it was «Rav Shimi bar Ashi» who objected: «But perhaps, whether» she gives him the money «in his presence or not in his presence,» if she gives it «with his consent, yes,» it is valid, but if she gives it «against his will,» it is «not» considered a valid act of giving. «And Hillel instituted what was necessary,» to remedy the practical occurrence that buyers would hide themselves at the end of the year. But even if the seller finds the buyer and the buyer refuses to accept payment, it would be necessary for Hillel to institute an ordinance.

moves.summary: from Hillel's ordinance: a conditional divorce paid against his will is not effective
moves.about: from Hillel's ordinance in the mishna: a conditional bill of divorce is effective only if she pays him with his consent, not against his will

moves.summary: the ordinance was needed only because ordinarily coerced giving does not count
moves.about: since Hillel needed a special ordinance to make coerced giving count, ordinarily coerced giving does not count

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב פפא, ואיתימא רב אשי
moves.summary: perhaps the ordinance concerned only giving not in his presence
moves.about: perhaps Hillel's ordinance was needed only for giving not in the buyer's presence, while in his presence coerced giving counts anyway

moves.summary: variant: from Hillel's ordinance, coerced giving counts; the ordinance was for giving not in his presence
moves.about: second version: from Hillel's ordinance, giving whether consensual or coerced counts, since the ordinance was needed only for giving not in the buyer's presence

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב פפא, ואיתימא רב שימי בר אשי
moves.summary: perhaps only consensual giving counts, and Hillel enacted only what was needed
moves.about: perhaps only consensual giving counts whether or not in his presence, and Hillel enacted only what the hiding buyers made necessary
